learning_outcomes.text: The student learns the notions necessary to understand the phenomena related to the motion of a fluid around a body, in particular for the study of the drag of vehicles, of the lifting surfaces and of the banding of some types of fluid machinery.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the course. Recall of vector calculus and fluid mechanics.

Bernoulli
					’s theorem for compressible fluids. Potential flows.
Two-dimensional flows: functions of complex variable. Conformal mapping.
Complex potential and velocity. Potential of uniform stream. Blasius' formulas. Kutta-Joukowski theorem.

Potential of a Source, a doublet and a vortex. Uniform stream around a circle. Lift. Joukowski
					’s Transformation. Flat plate, symmetric profile, general Joukowski profile.
Finite Wing: horseshoe vortex. Lift, downwash velocity and induced drag. Wings with minimum induced drag.

Boudary layer
					’s equations: laminar boundary layer along a flat plate. Turbulent boundary layer along a flat plate. Separation of boundary layer.
Compressible flows: subsonic and supersonic flows; linearized theory. Schock phenomena.
assessment_rules: The assessment is done through an oral test where the student explains concepts, demonstrations and principles regarding the behavior of bodies in a uniform stream. To pass, the student must demonstrate sufficient knowledge of all subjects without significant gaps. The calendar for oral tests is published on AlmaEsami.
